title: Position: Stop Anthropomorphizing Intermediate Tokens as Reasoning/Thinking Traces!
claim: Test-time scaling methods fall into two families: selectors that give no correctness guarantees, and verifiers that give full or partial guarantees.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, feedback loop arrow under bottom row
description: The figure has two horizontal rows of boxes joined by arrows, with the bold title 'Test-time scaling approaches' at the left between them. Each row starts with a small purple 'Prompt' box. An arrow leads to a yellow rounded box labeled "LLM' θ'". In the top row, the LLM fans out five arrows labeled 'Generate Multiple Answers' into a large blue 'Selector' box. The selector lists majority-based (self-consistency) and incremental (MCTS, beam search) methods. Its output goes to a gray 'Solution' box with a red 'No guarantees' tag. In the bottom row, the LLM sends a single arrow labeled 'Generate a candidate solution' into a blue 'Verifier' box. The verifier lists formal, learned and synthesized types. A 'Feedback' arrow loops from the verifier back to the LLM. The solution has a green 'Full/Partial Guarantees' tag. The eye goes first to the large blue boxes and the red and green tags.
caption: Test-time scaling approaches for teasing out reasoning
abstract: Intermediate token generation (ITG), where a model produces output before the solution, has become a standard method to improve the performance of language models on reasoning tasks. These intermediate tokens have been called \say{reasoning traces} or even \say{thinking traces} -- implicitly anthropomorphizing the traces, and implying that these traces resemble steps a human might take when solving a challenging problem, and as such can provide an interpretable window into the operation of the model's thinking process to the end user. In this position paper, we present evidence that this anthropomorphization isn't a harmless metaphor, and instead is quite dangerous -- it confuses the nature of these models and how to use them effectively, and leads to questionable research. We call on the community to avoid such anthropomorphization of intermediate tokens.
